The [[List of first overall National Football League Draft picks|first overall pick]] was [[Dave Parks]], an [[End (American and Canadian football)|end]] from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech]], selected by the [[1964 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]].{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=HM8zAAAAIBAJ&sjid=avcDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6961%2C128363 |newspaper=Spokane Daily Chronicle |agency=Associated Press |title=49er club tabs end for 1st draft choice |date=December 2, 1963 |page=20 }} The [[1964 American Football League draft|AFL draft]] was two days earlier, on Saturday, November 30.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=yN5YAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ePcDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5044%2C7512193 |newspaper=Spokane Daily Chronicle |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston picks QB to begin draft |date=November 30, 1963 |page=8}} In the next two years, the drafts were held on the same day; following the [[AFL–NFL merger|merger]] agreement in June 1966, a common draft was instituted for [[1967 NFL/AFL draft|1967]]. The 1964 NFL Draft is notable for the highest number of people enshrined in [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] with 11 total, 1 player selected was inducted as a coach, [[Bill Parcells]].{{cite news
